newWorkspaceDialog.description: A workspace is a team of bots on one shared computer. Its contacts, chats, logins and files are separate from every other workspace. Start one when a group of bots must not share this one's logins or files.

workspace.empty.intro: A workspace is a team of bots on one shared computer. Create one to get a computer, contacts and chats.
workspace.empty.title: No workspace yet
workspace.facts.intro: What the bots learned about this computer and the sites it reaches, written automatically with provenance and validity. Each bot's own experience is on its profile; task notes are on their chat.
workspace.intro: What every bot in {name} shares: one browser with one login state, one filesystem, one shell.
workspace.library.intro: Reviewed documents every bot on this computer can search. Bots propose; a human publishes. Facts a bot learned on its own live under Facts until a human promotes them here.
workspace.openInternet.label: open internet
workspace.openInternet.title: Allowlist is *: any public hostname
workspace.settings.aboutBody: A workspace is a team of bots on one shared computer. While {name} is selected in the sidebar, Chats and Contacts show only its chats and bots, and every bot in it can see what every other bot in it sees: the same logins, cookies and files. Two jobs that must not share a login or files go in two workspaces; the sidebar switcher creates one.
workspace.settings.aboutShort: Bots here share browser logins and files. Use a separate workspace for work that must stay isolated.
workspace.settings.allowedDomainsBody: This computer can reach only these hosts; everything else is blocked at the proxy, even for reading. A single * opens the public internet, which makes this an untrusted-browsing workspace that should hold no production credentials.
workspace.settings.botsNote: Instructions, schedules, model and approval rules are set on each bot's profile.
workspace.settings.domainsShort: Allow specific domains, or use * for the public internet. Open-internet workspaces should not hold production credentials.
